# Building

## The spine and its look

Build the opening, one middle chapter and the ending in two or three looks.
Let the person scroll those looks, ask which they choose, and stop for their
answer before building the remaining chapters. An unanswered question in
this turn is not a refusal to choose or permission to choose for them.

## The chapters and their words

After the look choice, build the remaining chapters. For the opening and
closing wording, show three versions of each whole beat, including the
surrounding fixed text. Recommend one and leave room for their own wording.
Stop for the choice, then use it word for word.

## The scene

Compare the running scene with the storyboard at its settled beats. With the captions hidden, does each scene show what the storyboard says it shows, rather than only names for it? Revise the composition when the explanation lives only in the surrounding prose. Keep that accessible prose; it does not replace what the scene was meant to show.

Inspect the changes between beats in both scroll directions, including intermediate positions. When words in the scene change, correct any overlap that makes the old and new words unreadable together. A readable settled beat does not establish a readable transition.

Read every word in the scene at the size it is shown on a desktop, a phone and a short screen. Words too small to read there go to the caption.
# Storyfolio engine

A starting project for one scroll and one story in 3D: shared pieces for what carries on
through the story, and a scene of its own for each chapter.
The supplied page is a placeholder that tests the engine: one sheet whose
picture changes by chapter. It has no design in it; replace all of `content/`.

Taken from V3 at `163b8ceb302b7b4e5beeff8f1161f4cdc7663b15` and made
independent of that site's content, paper shapes and assets. The source
project is unchanged. Storyfolio's engine and generated SVGs are MIT licensed.

## Start

Use Node 22.18 or later with native TypeScript support. Scaffold this folder
with `node <installed-skill>/scripts/scaffold.mjs <site-folder>`. Existing
`docs/story/` files are kept; any conflicting engine path aborts the copy.
Then, in the new site folder:

```bash
npm ci
npm run browsers
npm run dev
```

Open the local address printed by Next.js. Append `?look=dark` to choose a
look and `?fps` to show the frame meter. The appearance switch preserves
other query parameters, the fragment and the current scroll position.
Read the frame meter on a real phone; software rendering in a headless
browser does not measure phone performance.

Never install dependencies inside an installed skill. The copied project
belongs to the person, has its own lockfile, and does not depend on the
skill after scaffolding. System fonts make builds independent of remote
font services. Add licensed local files with `next/font/local` if needed;
the scene starts without waiting for them and redraws faces when fonts load.

## From storyboard to content

`lib/story/` contains pure, tested calculations. `components/story/` owns
the browser and scene. The person's story belongs in `content/`:

| File | Storyboard input |
|---|---|
| `story.ts` | Chapter IDs, names, roles, beat IDs and screen heights; one fixed piece count |
| `formations.ts` | A rest formation for every beat; optional `within` formation reached as its rest is scrolled |
| `faces.ts` | Pictures or canvas drawing functions for a beat and piece |
| `copy.ts` | Metadata, language, labels and complete HTML text |
| `looks.ts` | Ground, text and surface colors, lights and matte/no floor |
| `extras.ts` | Each chapter's own scene: lazy imports, each in its own error boundary |
| `links.ts` | Ordinary HTML links over a named piece at a named beat |
| `checks.json` | Optional checks of capabilities this fixture exercises |

Use `as const satisfies StoryDef` for the story and
`satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>` for formations. `checkStory`
also rejects invalid IDs, heights, piece counts and face references at
runtime. A formation contains one position, rotation and size per piece,
plus framing. `layouts.ts` supplies stack, fan, ring, grid, row and seeded
scatter; `measure` bounds their rotated faces. Depth, a custom shape's
extent and a whole formation's turn can require extra framing room.

The HTML in `app/page.tsx` follows the same beat order using `Chapter` and
`Beat`. A `Beat` can carry a static `fallback` image or diagram. Keep one
`h1`, stable chapter heading IDs and every factual claim in HTML. The check
script verifies the rendered beat IDs against the content contract.

The bundle type is in `components/story/types.ts`. Import a bundle inside a
client component, as `content/experience.tsx` does, and pass server-rendered
HTML as children. Bundles contain drawing functions and component loaders,
so cannot be serialized across a server/client prop boundary.

A custom `Piece` component receives its index, face material and look.
Build it at unit width/height centered at the origin. Its parent group gets
the formation's position, rotation and width/height scale each frame. Keep
materials present from the first frame. Extras receive the shared frame,
look, reduced-motion flag and control store and mount only near their
chapter. Their shapes are children of the formation group.

Use `useExtraFrame` from `components/story/extra-frame.tsx` for an extra's
frame callback. It receives the same state, delta and optional XR frame as
React Three Fiber's `useFrame`. A synchronous exception disables that
callback immediately and unmounts its owning extra, leaving the core scene,
other extras and HTML running. Each extra also has a React boundary for
render failures and rejected lazy imports. For example:

```tsx
useExtraFrame(() => {
  if (line.current) line.current.visible = frameRef.current.from === 1;
});
```

`content/extras/middle-line.tsx` uses this hook. A raw third-party `useFrame`
callback, timer, event handler or rejected asynchronous task does not pass
through this guard. Handle failures at those boundaries explicitly;
wrapping a component in a React boundary does not catch them.

For caption controls, use `useControl` or `useControls` from
`components/story/controls.tsx` in a client component. Real controls remain
HTML. The canvas takes no pointer events. Overlay links are hidden and
removed from keyboard navigation outside their beat; supply the same
destination in the text for fallback access.

For a sketch, add a client component importing its own bundle and HTML to
`content/sketches/index.ts`. Its key becomes `/sketch/<id>`. The initial
registry is empty and unknown keys return 404.

## Check

```bash
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run check
```

`check` builds, starts its own production server on a free local port,
runs the browser matrix and stops only that process group. It writes a
manifest, logs, reports and screenshots under `checks/<timestamp>/` and
returns a failure exit code for failed checks. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`
selects an optional shared browser cache. `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE` is an optional
override; normally the installed local package provides the browser tool.

The matrix checks both looks at wide, short and phone sizes, reduced
motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript. Optional plain-story probes exercise
keyboard access and failed chapter loading. Context loss checks the HTML
fallback. Wide captures include the beginning, middle and end of each
beat's rest; reduced-motion captures also check that a stationary scene
stays still. Open every screenshot for overlap, clipping, legibility and
framing. Automatic passes do not replace visual review.

For a focused investigation use `npm run check -- --only=light-phone`.
`--skip-build` checks a previously built app and is diagnostic only.
Neither establishes a fresh full acceptance run. `scripts/shoot.mjs`
documents individual screenshots, blocked requests, look switching,
overflow and shader checks.

No JavaScript leaves the server-rendered text. No WebGL or a failed scene
leaves ordinary text and any beat's static image. Reduced motion cuts
between poses, including within-beat formations, without idle movement.
The scene pauses offscreen, caps sharpness on touch devices and steps down
quality when measured frames stay slow.
# Working on this site

Read `docs/story/handover.md` first, if it exists. Keep it current with the
person's words, decisions, implementation and check results. Keep all
lasting context in this repository and commit it with the work.

This starter uses Next.js 16. Before using an unfamiliar API, read the
relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` if provided by the installed
package, otherwise consult the official Next.js documentation for that
version. Do not assume older examples apply.

Install dependencies with `npm ci`, install Chromium with `npm run browsers`,
then run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run check`.
The last command builds and checks a production server. Open its screenshots
before calling a visual change done. Read `README.md` for the content
contract and where the results are written.

The plain story is a test of the engine. Replace it from the person's
approved storyboard and confirmed facts. Keep the text complete without
the scene, and test reduced motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript.

# Storyboard — The open runbook

Status: proposed script, awaiting Dawit's approval. Concept 01 chosen by assistant at Dawit's explicit request on 22 October 2026; rationale recorded in concepts.md. This document defines scenes, factual coverage and behaviour, not finished captions. Working chapter/beat labels below are editorial navigation labels. Final whole-beat wording comes at the later wording checkpoint.

## The thread

A bound runbook opens into the library where Dawit came to software. Its leaves bend into a route, support a reading stand, open into working documents and raise five different work miniatures. At the close those fold into one complete book with a contact invitation and CV leaf. The binding and paper behaviour connect the chapters; the scene subjects change with the story. No repeated wall of project cards, decorative server racks or anonymous points-as-data.

The opening begins with Dawit's library work and the 2014 outage account. The closing brings the runbook, cutover checklist and rollback plan together, recalling the confirmed reason he cares about rollbacks. There is no rhetorical question or implied promise of incident-free migrations. The complete book is a visual ending, not a claim that the 2014 table or a real system was restored.

All geometry is an illustration, visibly labelled. No photographs, screenshots, copied covers, actual employer diagrams, slide reproductions, actual runbook text or actual commands. No assets to acquire or additional skills to install.

## Chapter map

| 2 / #places | Three places | Addis Ababa, Amsterdam, Rotterdam | Grew up and studied in Addis; moves in 2016 and 2020 | Paper route relief between three labelled place markers | Chapter links; next-chapter anchor |

## The first thirty seconds

The first screen carries Dawit's name, a plain-language description of migration work as moving or changing systems, and one proof: the runbook first version/continuing ownership and its use by 40 teams. The everyday meaning of cutover (changing which system is in use) and rollback (a way to return to an earlier state) is provided where those terms first appear; these are generic explanations, not promises about real systems. Avoid the unconfirmed formal role title.

The catalogue/library origin is pictured immediately; the 2014 account gets the next short beat rather than occupying the whole first screen. A visible contact shortcut, CV link and chapter navigation make the site usable without following the scroll. On phone, reserve enough initial space for name, work and proof; geometry scales down before those move out of view. The concept sketch's generous mobile illustration height is not a requirement to preserve in the final opening.

## Navigation and five detail pages

Normal document scrolling; no scroll hijacking, forced progression, scroll lock or required gesture. Stable heading IDs and URLs. Desktop shows all seven chapter links; phone uses an ordinary HTML disclosure for those links plus an always-visible contact shortcut. A skip link goes to contact. Focus indicators, usable tap targets and labels for every control; no canvas-only interaction.

Project summaries are present in HTML on their corresponding beats. Each opens a separate local page in the same tab, with a meaningful URL, one h1, a back-to-projects link and the same contact/CV access. This gives usable browser Back, deep links, keyboard navigation and no-JavaScript behaviour without modal complexity. Decorative scene objects do not need to be clickable; adjacent HTML links are authoritative.

| Local route | Expanded material allowed | Deliberate limits |
|---|---|---|
| /work/migration | Scope of availability, measured figure, full 26-month window, both internal incidents and their under-ten-minute durations; generic model with forward/reverse controls and plain text equivalent | No zero-downtime claim, 310-service count, exact architecture, actual migration procedure or unsupported personal attribution |
| /work/database-upgrade | Larger labelled database illustration with an accessible static cutaway view; work topic identified as database upgrade | Briefest detail: no additional personal technical narrative is confirmed. Do not pad it with versions, capacity, technique, outcomes or backend explanations. The click adds visual detail, not guessed case-study claims |
| /work/runbook | First-version authorship; continuing ownership; use by 40 teams; enlarged illustrative document | No internal content, specific stage sequence, sole authorship of all versions or adoption timeframe |
| /work/ferry | Former-colleague creation credit; maintenance since 2022; Dawit's cutover command contribution; enlarged illustrative command display | No fake runnable command, stars, GitHub link from placeholder URL, adoption or implementation claims |
| /work/talk | Talk opening built around the confirmed 2014 account; generic stage illustration; conference-organiser contact | No downloaded slides/video, unconfirmed title/event/year/link, invented talk outline or quotation |

The database limitation is a planned factual boundary, not a request for another factual round. The public page simply stays brief; it does not display editorial notes about unconfirmed claims. The same rule applies to missing external links on ferry and the talk.

## Contact and printable HTML CV

Use an ordinary mailto:dawit@example.com link. The site sends nothing. No form, chat, scheduling integration, analytics or mail service. The example address is explicitly authorized as public contact; never replace it with a guessed real address.

/cv is a readable HTML CV with local print styling. A Download HTML CV link serves a self-contained dawit-bekele-cv.html file with embedded styles, no script, no remote fonts/assets and no dependency on a running server once saved. View/print and download are separate, clearly named links. Browser printing remains available with JavaScript disabled; a small print button may enhance it when JavaScript works.

CV content: name; authorized email; migration-work focus and 2027 independent plan; confirmed career milestones (library catalogue work; Amsterdam/Lumen move in 2016 and its one permitted work line; Rotterdam/Kestrel move in 2020); degree/institution/years; confirmed migration scope/figure/incidents if included together; runbook authorship/ownership/adoption; shared on-call result with scope and “we”; ferry maintenance/contribution/creator credit; talk opening account if relevant. No unconfirmed formal titles, full employment ranges, skill inventories, database specifications or talk identifiers. Use milestone years rather than inventing tenure end dates. Biography and work share one source of confirmed content so CV and page do not disagree. No PDF conversion service needed.

## Without the scene

All substantive text, navigation, work links and contact/CV remain ordinary server-rendered HTML. The scene is an enhancement with an accessible label, not a reading surface or source of exclusive facts.

| Case | Visitor experience |
|---|---|
| Phone | Compact scene above flowing text; chapter-specific static/framed composition; no text overlay on moving objects. Normal scrolling, responsive line lengths, touch-friendly controls and all five work links. Geometry and pixel density reduced before text is compromised |
| Reduced motion | Discrete scene poses at beat boundaries; no fly-through, continuous curl, idle motion or automatic token travel. Model state can change through explicit buttons, without animated interpolation. All content and controls remain available |
| No WebGL, context loss or a failed scene/chapter | Labelled local static illustrations beside the same HTML, plus normal navigation. A scene failure is contained; it cannot remove the text, links or other chapters. No repeated error notices competing with the story |
| No JavaScript | The entire story, detail pages, CV/download, ordinary disclosure navigation and mailto render as HTML. Static locally generated illustrations stand in for 3D; no animated spacing gaps, loading spinner or essential hidden disclosure |
| Paused illustration | A plain pause/enable-3D control can choose static illustrations while retaining document scroll. It never disables navigation or text. Offscreen rendering pauses automatically |

Static alternatives will be locally generated drawings of the same subjects, sized explicitly with useful alt text. No actual employer topology in either 3D or static form. Purely decorative geometry is hidden from assistive technology; controls and explanations remain in HTML.

## Two material looks to compare in the runnable spine

The concept selection does not decide the look. Build these two for opening, a working middle and closing before asking Dawit to choose by scrolling.

| Look | Ground | Ink | One accent | Surfaces and light |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper / daylight | Warm linen #EEE9DC | Charcoal green #283532 | Bookcloth rust #BC542F | Ivory paper, rust cloth binding, soft matte shadows and broad daylight |
| Desk / lamplight | Dark desk #172321 | Warm ivory #F3EDDF | Copper #DA9A71 | Cream paper with dark cloth binding, controlled warm light and low-glare matte surfaces |

Text uses the local system sans-serif stack (system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif). Document labels/annotations use the local system monospace stack (ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace). No webfonts. These are two typographic roles; actual installed fonts vary by machine. Only short, legible document labels appear in the scene; paragraphs and figures stay HTML. Test text contrast in both looks. No bright emissive paper or obligatory glass effect.

## Everything else

| Item | Build, later or never | Decision and concrete scope |
|---|---|---|
| Way round the page | Build | User asked ordinary navigation; assistant specifies seven chapter anchors, visible contact and CV, mobile HTML disclosure, skip link, back-to-top and project return links |
| Page for each project | Build | User asked more on click; assistant chooses five standalone local routes rather than dialogs |
| Every project listed | Build | User names exactly five; each gets one concise HTML beat and detail link |
| Contact and CV | Build | User: public example mailto only, printable downloadable HTML CV. Assistant specifies /cv plus self-contained download |
| Testimonials | Never | User: none; leave out |
| Language | Build English only | User; no language selector or translations |
| Share preview | Build local; public URL later | User requests preview; assistant specifies local 1200×630 image generated from own runbook geometry and name/work text, plus matching metadata. No fake public domain/canonical URL; share URL, image absolute URL and live crawler check wait for publishing choice |
| Site icon | Build | User requests icon; assistant specifies a simple locally drawn open-book/DB mark, SVG plus appropriate local raster fallback. No external icon pack |
| Missing-page page | Build | User requests useful page; assistant specifies friendly English message, Home, Work and Contact links plus CV access; real 404 status, no forced redirect or scene dependency |
| Page titles and descriptions | Build | Assistant: per-page title/description, semantic headings and consistent local navigation. No unsupported structured credentials, fake social profiles or SEO claims |
| Blog | Never | User |
| Chat | Never | User |
| Translation | Never | User |
| Contact form / mail sending | Never | User |
| Tracking / analytics / third-party embeds | Never in this local build | Assistant: none needed for the authorized scope; change only on a later request |
| Legal notice | Later | User explicitly defers legal and hosting details until choosing to publish; no invented address or jurisdiction text |
| Hosting, deployment, domain, sitemap/public canonical | Later | User retains publishing decision. No account, upload, remote repo or publishing task now. Leave local builds noindex |
| External asset purchase/download and additional skills | Never for this build | User explicitly declined. Available tools, own geometry and local fonts only |
| Old site's replacement | Later at publishing | User permits replacement; local site prepares for that without changing any live site |

The local preview image and icon are site features, not a publishing step. A local image/metadata preview can be inspected without a public share service. All browser requests should stay on the local origin.

## Build and review sequence after this script is approved

1. Build a runnable spine: opening/library origin, working migration middle and complete-book contact ending, in both material looks. Present them for Dawit's look choice.
2. Build remaining chapter scenes and all requested supporting pages/features from this script. Present three whole-beat wording versions at the wording checkpoint; keep source claims identical across versions.
3. Run type/lint/tests and the production browser matrix, including desktop/short/phone, both looks, reduced motion, no WebGL, no JavaScript, links, CV download/print and real 404. Inspect screenshots for each beat. Verify scene failures preserve HTML; no external requests; no overflow. Software-rendered browser success does not establish real-phone frame rate.
4. Present local review addresses and known limitations; record Dawit's actual review. No publishing.

## Approval requested

Approve this script or name changes to chapter order, scene subjects or the proposed features. Approval applies to structure and factual scope; final look and final whole-beat wording remain separate choices. No new facts or assets are required to proceed after approval.
